findings.location: <div class="lyrics"> (3rd stanza, line 2) — hymn text: "Crown Him, ye morning stars of light, / Who fixed this floating ball, / Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might, / And crown Him Lord of all!"
findings.source_quote: Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the English sense accurately. A faithful Urdu rendering would convey an exhortation to praise or acclaim Israel’s strong One (the Strength of Israel). Suggested Urdu: "اُس اسرائیل کی قوت کو اب سلام کرو" or "اب اسرائیل کی طاقت کو سلام کرو" — preserving the exhortation 'hail' (سلام کرو/سلام پیش کرو) rather than 'lesson' or 'سابق'.
findings.translation_quote: "اب اسرائیل کی قوت کا سبق قبول کرو," (uses 'سبق' = 'lesson', which changes meaning and omits the exhortation to 'hail')

findings.location: Opening Scripture line (first paragraph, emphasized quote)
findings.source_quote: for thy pleasure they are and were created
findings.suggested_fix: The Urdu phrase used ("اور وہ تیرے مشنّتِ خاطر ہیں") uses 'مشنّت' which is non-idiomatic and unclear. Use an idiomatic Urdu rendering that preserves the sense 'created for thy pleasure' such as: "اور وہ تیرے لطف کے لیے پیدا کیے گئے ہیں" or "اور وہ تیرے لطف کے سبب پیدا ہوئے تھے".
findings.translation_quote: "اور وہ تیرے مشنّتِ خاطر ہیں اور پیدا ہوئیں — مکاشفہ 4:11۔" (uses 'مشنّتِ' which is not standard Urdu and may obscure meaning)
